comparator.name: Linguistics (Taalwetenschap)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 catalogue supports 175 distinct EC in the selected Descriptive Linguistics route. The same 5 EC Berber module appears in years two and three. The archived transition notice describes a rotation with Leti, but the current sources do not establish which module satisfies the remaining requirement for September 2026 entrants. The zero-credit thesis seminar is separate from the 10 EC thesis.
components: Language and Culture of the Indo-Europeans

routeSelection.basis: Descriptive Linguistics is a current formal route and the existing neutral selection remains valid. Differing route order across current official presentations is not used to change it, and UCR fit was not considered.

exception.reason: The current curriculum lists the same 5 EC Berber course in years two and three. An earlier transition notice describes an alternation with Leti. Leiden’s current sources do not yet confirm how September 2026 entrants complete the remaining 5 EC.
exception.curriculumContext: The documented requirements and eligible choices account for 175 distinct EC. They include a 10 EC thesis with a separate seminar and 30 EC of open electives.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Linguistics degree studies how languages are structured, how they change, and how people acquire and use them. In Descriptive Linguistics, students compare languages and learn to analyse and document them through fieldwork.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The table shows 175 distinct credits in the Descriptive Linguistics route. The current catalogue lists the same Berber course in two years. A separate 5 EC requirement still needs confirmation before a complete comparison can be made.

curriculum.limitation: The degree requires 180 EC. The first year offers course sets in Dutch or English, and the Descriptive Linguistics specialisation is taught in English.
